rows.body: Core Radisson under Choice Hotels is positioned as a global upscale flag with visible CALA momentum—especially Mexico, Central America, Panama, and the Caribbean—alongside airport, urban conversion, and secondary-city full-service entries where distribution and a recognizable mainstream brand matter more than lifestyle sub-brand storytelling.

rows.title: Americas
rows.body:
Established presence

North America remains the scale anchor for the Radisson portfolio; owner conversations often start with conversion economics, loyalty attach, and how the flag competes against other upscale boxes in gateway and regional-hub markets.

rows.title: CALA
rows.body:
Strong CALA momentum

Recent core Radisson openings in Mexico, Panama, and Suriname illustrate Choice CALA’s push in urban greenfield, airport, beach conversion, and historic downtown repositioning—not Radisson Blu or RED.

rows.title: Europe
rows.body:
Mature global footprint

Europe remains core to the Radisson brand heritage and network density; for many owners it is the reference set for brand standards, conversion playbooks, and loyalty scale—even when the live deal is elsewhere.

rows.title: MEA
rows.body:
Selective / market-specific

Growth is uneven by country and access; evaluate owner strategy, operator depth, and fee stack before treating MEA as interchangeable with CALA or Americas conversion narratives.

rows.title: APAC
rows.body:
High relevance in key gateways

APAC matters for owners weighing international distribution in gateway cities and mixed-use corridors; proof points are market-specific—do not assume U.S. or European ramp curves.

Urban conversion and repositioning

CALA secondary-city greenfield

Meetings-capable urban entries
Coastal and leisure conversions (core Radisson)

Radisson’s growth profile under Choice is conversion- and distribution-led: the brand compounds when owners need a recognizable upscale flag, clear operating standards, and portfolio retail—not a one-off soft brand with ambiguous QA or fee story. Use public CALA openings as directional proof of where the network is leaning, not as property-level performance guarantees.

Radisson’s footprint reads as “global upscale with CALA momentum and conversion DNA”: large enough for Choice distribution and loyalty credibility, still positioned as a mainstream full-service flag versus rigid prototype or lifestyle sub-brand theater. It tends to show best where owners need recognizable upscale positioning, operating standards, and network retail—not a bespoke luxury operating story.
